info.title: AyiPM API
info.description:
The API behind the AyiPM web app. Successful responses are `{ "data": ... }` and errors are `{ "error": "message" }`.

Most endpoints need a signed-in session. Sign in with `POST /api/auth/login` (or `POST /api/setup` on a new workspace); the browser keeps the session cookie and sends it with every later request, including the ones you try out here.

put.summary: Replace the projects this person belongs to
put.description: Returns every project, since several may have changed.

post.summary: Move a task to a column and position on the board
post.description: Used for drag and drop. Returns every task in the target column.

get.summary: Check whether the workspace still needs to be set up

post.summary: Create the workspace and its owner account, and sign in as the owner
post.description: Works only once; after that it fails with 409.

post.summary: Issue a one-time password reset link
post.description: Emails the link to the person when email is set up. The admin can also share it themselves.

post.summary: Issue a fresh invitation link for someone who hasn't joined yet

get.summary: Look up a password reset link by its token

post.summary: Set a new password with a reset link's token
Sign in with an email or Employee ID
post.description: Sets the session cookie, which the browser then sends with every request.

post.summary: Finish signing in with an authenticator or recovery code
Start two-factor setup during sign-in, when the workspace requires it
Confirm two-factor setup during sign-in, and sign in

get.summary: Look up an invitation by its token

post.summary: Accept an invitation by choosing a password, and sign in
Ask an admin for a password reset link
post.description: Marks the person's profile as Reset requested.

delete.summary: Reset your preferences to the defaults

ayipm_session.description: The session cookie set when you sign in. It is httpOnly, so there is nothing to enter under Authorize: sign in with `POST /api/auth/login` and the browser sends it for you.
